answer: Cap seat throughput per epoch, not per identity. A farm can scatter fake heads like yarrow across a tundra — cheap and endless — but only a fixed number K of grace elevations clear each close, so inflating identities never multiplies seats; it only stretches each head's expected wait to ~M/K epochs. Every forged signup scratched out with the same quill competes for those same K slots. Aggregate yield stays pinned to K, so the attacker pays in real elapsed time per captured seat, and no pile of cheap identities compresses wall-clock time.
